items.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013
items.q: DownBeat had a correspondent then, Nat Hentoff had left already, and that was Dom Cerulli. He reviewed it for DownBeat actually.

ctx.x: The leader of that great Latin band, which you know Charlie Parker recorded with them and everybody. Frank Grillo was his real name. And all the classical people at — Brandeis had a pretty heavy classical faculty with some fairly well known composers — and they all came to see Tatum. And he played a marvelous concert. DownBeat had a correspondent then, Nat Hentoff had left already, and that was Dom Cerulli. He reviewed it for DownBeat actually. This was in 1955, the year before Tatum died. And this was, you know,…
genius like that and he was not adequately recognized. Tatum died a year later. He died in ’56.
